threat_event: Firmware signing key is stolen, misused, or lost, so an attacker can sign malicious firmware or the company can no longer update units
threat_source: Cybercriminal or insider; laptop loss or failure
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Key is a password-protected file on one laptop with one USB backup; one person can sign; no HSM; no second approval
existing_controls: Laptop full-disk encryption and EDR; key file password; USB copy in the office safe
treatment_plan: Move the signing key into an HSM-backed key in the cloud key management service; two-person approval for every signing; signing only through the release pipeline; documented key ceremony and backup; no release outside the lab until done

threat_event: Attacker on a hospital network uses the shared hub maintenance password or the shared API key to change alarm defaults or impersonate hubs
threat_source: Cybercriminal or curious insider at a customer site
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Same maintenance password on every hub; one API key per environment compiled into firmware; key also leaked in CI logs (R-023) and stored unencrypted on the hub, readable through the debug serial port (P07)
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-08; hub fleet after clearance; SYS-04 ingestion API
existing_controls: Hubs at the simulation center sit on an isolated, monitored test network; TLS to the cloud
treatment_plan: Unique per-device maintenance credentials set at the contract manufacturer; per-device certificates for hub-to-cloud; maintenance page off by default and reachable only from the hub's service port; rotate the current API key

threat_event: The 510(k) is placed on hold or delayed because the cybersecurity documentation is incomplete
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No threat model beyond the radio link; no SBOM; no cybersecurity management plan or CVD; no penetration test
existing_controls: Regulatory consultant engaged; guidance checklist started
treatment_plan: Complete the P03 premarket readiness roadmap: threat model, SBOM, management plan with CVD, security testing, and a pre-submission meeting in 2026-11 to confirm the approach

threat_event: Nearby attacker intercepts or injects sensor data over BLE, so the hub shows wrong vital signs
threat_source: Attacker with radio equipment within range
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Sensor-to-hub pairing uses the unauthenticated "Just Works" method; no application-layer authentication or replay protection
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-08 sensor-hub link; patient monitoring after clearance
existing_controls: Short radio range; hub flags sensor disconnects
treatment_plan: Authenticated pairing plus application-layer message authentication and replay protection; add to the threat model and fuzz the BLE interface

threat_event: A known exploited vulnerability in a third-party component (embedded Linux, BLE stack, TLS library) goes unnoticed and ships in the device
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No SBOM; component spreadsheet has no versions; no monitoring of NVD, supplier advisories, or the CISA KEV catalog
existing_controls: Dependency alerts on cloud code only
treatment_plan: Generate a machine-readable SBOM for sensor, hub, and cloud in every CI build; add support status and end-of-support dates; weekly monitoring against NVD and the KEV catalog with records

threat_event: Source code and design files are stolen through a compromised account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Repository and eQMS reachable from anywhere; no log review; contractor access not removed
existing_controls: MFA on repository and suite; code review
treatment_plan: Account checklist and monthly review (R-011); monthly log review of repository clones and permission changes

threat_event: Ransomware on a laptop or lab workstation stops engineering work and encrypts local test data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Lab workstations have no EDR and are unpatched; flat lab network
existing_controls: EDR and patching on laptops; code and records in SaaS
treatment_plan: Add lab workstations to the MSP contract (EDR, patching, named logins); separate lab network (R-016)

threat_event: Attacker takes over the cloud tenant through the shared owner account and deletes the environment or tampers with the update service
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared owner account known to two people; owner rights used for daily work; no log review
existing_controls: MFA on named accounts; device signature check protects against tampered images
treatment_plan: Break-glass owner account in the safe; named least-privilege roles; alerts on owner-role use; monthly review

threat_event: The provisioning file or firmware images are exposed or altered at the contract manufacturer
threat_source: Attacker targeting the supplier, or supplier staff error
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Quality agreement has no security terms; files sent by a shared link that never expires; test station security unknown
existing_controls: Device verifies firmware signatures at first boot
treatment_plan: Security terms in the quality agreement (secret handling, test station controls, 72-hour incident notice); authenticated transfer with expiry; security questions at the Q4 supplier audit

threat_event: A researcher or the partner hospital finds a WM-1 vulnerability and discloses it publicly because there is no way to report it
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No CVD policy; no published security contact; no intake procedure
affected_asset_or_process: BP-08; reputation with partner and investors
existing_controls: Website contact form reaches the CEO
treatment_plan: Publish CVD policy and security contact with 3-business-day acknowledgment; intake in the eQMS; join an ISAO that shares medical device vulnerability information

threat_event: A former employee or contractor uses access that was never removed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Offboarding by email to the MSP; repository, eQMS, and cloud accounts not on any checklist
existing_controls: MFA tied to the person's phone
treatment_plan: Offboarding checklist covering every system on the last day; expiry dates on contractor accounts; monthly reconciliation. Former contractor's access removed 2026-08-11 (P07)

threat_event: Business email compromise diverts a contract manufacturer payment or investor funds
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No payment verification rule; no phishing training
existing_controls: MFA on email
treatment_plan: Call-back verification on any change to bank details; phishing training and quarterly simulations

threat_event: Design history records are lost or corrupted in the eQMS
threat_source: eQMS vendor failure or deletion by error
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No company-held export; vendor backups not evidenced
existing_controls: Vendor platform backups per contract
treatment_plan: Quarterly full export of the eQMS to company storage; request the vendor's SOC 2 report

threat_event: The one person who can sign firmware or administer the cloud is unavailable during an urgent release
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Only the Head of Engineering can sign; only the Cloud Software Engineer administers the tenant; nothing written down
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Two named signers under the two-person rule (R-001); release runbook; second cloud administrator (the Head of Engineering) with named access

threat_event: The cloud service cannot be restored after deletion or corruption, and recovery targets for the clinical service are never set
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Snapshots kept 7 days and never restore-tested; environment built by hand; no recovery targets for the post-clearance service
existing_controls: Daily database snapshots
treatment_plan: Define the environment as code; first restore test by 2026-10-31; set clinical-service RTO and RPO in the design inputs before design freeze

threat_event: A compromised lab workstation reaches office laptops and pre-production units on the flat network
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Lab network flat with office; lab workstations unmanaged, unpatched, shared login
existing_controls: Firewall blocks inbound traffic from the internet
treatment_plan: Separate lab network segment; lab workstations under MSP management with named logins

threat_event: Source code or unfixed vulnerability details pasted into public AI chatbots are retained or exposed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No approved AI tools list; engineers use personal chatbot accounts
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: POL-04 AI rule: no Restricted data in unapproved AI tools; evaluate an enterprise coding assistant with a no-training term (P10 AI-003)

threat_event: AI-001 respiratory rate estimates are less accurate for some patients (skin tone, body size, bedding, position), so deterioration is missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Feasibility model trained on one licensed dataset with unknown demographic mix; no subgroup testing plan
regulatory_driver: FD&C Act and 21 CFR 820.10(c) design controls; N31-33-R05 (524B(b)(2))
existing_controls: Feature not in WM-1; camera disabled in firmware
treatment_plan: Bias testing plan and subgroup thresholds before any design input freeze for AI-001 (see P10)

threat_event: The AI-001 training dataset cannot be used commercially or was collected without adequate consent
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: License terms not reviewed; dataset contains video of research participants
existing_controls: Dataset used for feasibility only
treatment_plan: Counsel reviews the license and consent scope; stop use if commercial use is excluded; plan own data collection under IRB oversight (P10)

threat_event: Hurricane closes the office and lab for several days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single office and lab; units and signing key backup in the office
existing_controls: SaaS systems reachable from anywhere; laptops go home
treatment_plan: Accepted: engineering continues remotely on SaaS; before a storm, the Head of Engineering takes the signing key backup and 4 lab units off site. Residual risk is schedule slip of days

threat_event: After clearance the company cannot deliver security patches on a justified regular cycle or out of cycle
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No patch cycle, no out-of-cycle procedure, no measurement of field update adoption
existing_controls: Hubs accept signed over-the-air updates; sensors update through the hub
treatment_plan: Write the patch timelines into the cybersecurity management plan (quarterly regular cycle; out-of-cycle path for critical vulnerabilities); measure time to patch and field adoption

threat_event: An evaluation hub at the simulation center is used as a foothold into the partner hospital's test network
threat_source: Cybercriminal or tester at the hospital
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared maintenance password; hubs run embedded Linux with a web service
existing_controls: Hospital test network is isolated and monitored by the hospital security team
treatment_plan: Disable the maintenance page on evaluation units by configuration; tell the hospital security team (done 2026-08-14)

threat_event: Anyone with repository read access copies the hub API key from CI build logs
threat_source: Former contractor, compromised account, or curious insider
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: A debug step printed the key in build logs; logs kept 90 days; readable by all members (found in P07 testing)
existing_controls: CI secret masking (bypassed by the debug step)
treatment_plan: Remove the debug step and purge logs (done 2026-08-12); rotate the key in all environments and reflash units; per-device certificates (R-002)

threat_event: A laptop is lost or stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops travel with staff
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; EDR; MSP can wipe; data in SaaS
treatment_plan: Accepted: encrypted devices and SaaS-held data leave little exposure. The signing key laptop is covered by R-001
